title: Overnight Oats with Mixed Berries
ingredients: ½ cup rolled oats (use certified gluten‐free oats if needed)
½ cup milk (almond, oat, soy, or dairy milk)
¼ cup Greek yogurt (or dairy‑free alternative for vegan)
½ cup mixed berries (blueberries, strawberries, raspberries)
substitutions: Substitute with dairy‑free yogurt and an alternative milk for nut allergies.
instructions: In an airtight jar, combine the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds, honey, and salt.
Stir in the mixed berries.
Seal and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours) so the oats soften and flavors blend.
Stir well in the morning and enjoy straight from the jar or transfer to a bowl.
mealPreppingTip: Multiply the ingredients into several mason jars for a quick grab‐and‐go breakfast during the week.

title: Veggie & Cheese Egg Muffins
ingredients: ½ cup diced bell peppers (any color)
½ cup shredded cheese (cheddar or dairy‑free alternative)
1 tsp olive oil (for greasing the muffin tin)
substitutions: Use a plant‑based egg substitute and dairy‑free cheese for a vegan version.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
In a bowl, whisk the eggs and season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the diced vegetables and cheese.
Lightly grease a muffin tin with olive oil and fill each cup about ¾ full with the egg mixture.
Bake for 18–20 minutes until set.
Let cool and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
mealPreppingTip: These muffins can be kept in the fridge for up to 4–5 days. Reheat in the microwave for a quick breakfast.

title:
Avocado Toast 
 Variations
ingredients: 2 slices whole grain or gluten‑free bread
Optional toppings: cherry tomatoes, radish slices, microgreens, smoked salmon, or a sprinkle of chickpeas
substitutions: Use gluten‑free bread; replace smoked salmon with extra veggies or chickpea mash for vegan options.
instructions: Toast the bread slices to your preferred crispness.
In a small bowl, mash the avocado with lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Spread the avocado mixture evenly on the toasted bread.
Top with your chosen optional ingredients and serve immediately.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare the avocado mash ahead of time and store it in an airtight container with a thin layer of olive oil to help prevent browning. Toast your slices fresh.

title: Greek Yogurt Parfait with Granola & Fruit
ingredients: ⅓ cup granola (choose a nut‑free version if needed)
½ cup mixed fresh fruits (berries, sliced banana, kiwi)
substitutions: Use dairy‑free yogurt and nut‑free granola when necessary.
instructions: In a glass or bowl, layer half of the yogurt, then add a layer of mixed fruit.
Sprinkle granola over the fruit.
Add the remaining yogurt and top with another layer of fruit.
Drizzle with honey or maple syrup if desired, then serve immediately.
mealPreppingTip: Assemble parfait layers in small jars and pack granola separately to maintain texture.

title: Chia Pudding with Mango and Coconut Milk
ingredients: 1 cup coconut milk (or substitute with another non‑dairy milk for coconut allergy)
substitutions: Use almond, soy, or oat milk if there is a coconut allergy (consider nut‑free options as needed).
instructions: In a bowl or jar, combine the chia seeds, coconut milk, maple syrup, and vanilla extract. Stir well.
Let the mixture sit for 5 minutes and stir again to prevent clumping.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Top with diced mango before serving.
mealPreppingTip: Make a batch in individual jars for up to several days, stirring briefly before serving.

title: Breakfast Burrito Bowl with Black Beans and Rice
ingredients: ½ cup black beans (rinsed and drained)
2 scrambled eggs (or tofu scramble for vegan)
¼ tsp cumin and chili powder each
substitutions: Use tofu scramble for a vegan alternative.
instructions: In a bowl, lay down the cooked brown rice as the base.
Top with black beans, scrambled eggs (or tofu scramble), and diced bell peppers.
Sprinkle with cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper.
Drizzle salsa over the top and add the avocado slices.
Toss lightly just before eating to combine flavors.
mealPreppingTip: Pack each component separately in a container to reheat and assemble quickly when ready to eat.

title:
Banana Almond 
Pancakes
ingredients: ½ cup almond flour (or oat flour for a nut‑free option)
Cooking spray or a small amount of oil for the pan
substitutions: Use oat flour to eliminate nuts and an egg replacer for a vegan option if desired.
instructions: In a bowl, mix mashed banana, beaten eggs, almond (or oat) flour, baking powder, milk, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Heat a non‑stick skillet over medium heat and coat lightly with oil or cooking spray.
Pour about ¼ cup of batter per pancake into the skillet.
Cook until bubbles form on the surface, roughly 2 minutes, then flip and cook for an additional 1–2 minutes until golden brown on both sides.
Serve with fresh fruit or drizzle with maple syrup.
mealPreppingTip: Make a larger batch, let cool completely, then store in an airtight container in the fridge. Reheat in a toaster or microwave for busy mornings.

title: Protein-Packed Quinoa Porridge
ingredients: 2 tbsp chopped nuts (optional; check allergen warnings)
substitutions: Use dairy‑free milk and omit or substitute nuts if allergic.
instructions: In a small saucepan, combine the cooked quinoa and milk. Warm gently over medium heat until heated through.
Stir in the protein powder and cinnamon until fully blended.
Remove from heat and sweeten with honey or maple syrup.
Top with fresh berries and chopped nuts if using.
mealPreppingTip: Portion into individual containers for a hearty breakfast that can be quickly reheated in the microwave.

title:
Baked Oatmeal 
Cups
ingredients: 2 cups rolled oats (use gluten‑free oats if needed)
substitutions: Use an egg substitute, dairy‑free milk, and omit nuts to suit allergies.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C) and grease a muffin tin or line with paper liners.
In a large bowl, mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt.
In another bowl, whisk together the eggs, milk, maple syrup, and vanilla extract.
Combine the wet and dry ingredients until just mixed.
Gently fold in berries (and nuts if using).
Distribute the mixture evenly into the muffin tin, filling each cup about ¾ full.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the edges are lightly browned.
mealPreppingTip: These oatmeal cups can be refrigerated for up to 5 days or frozen in an airtight container for longer storage.

title:
Spinach & Veggie 
Frittata
ingredients: ½ cup diced red bell pepper
⅓ cup shredded cheese (optional; dairy or non‑dairy)
substitutions: For a vegan version, use a chickpea flour “frittata” base (about 1 cup chickpea flour mixed with ¼ cup water per serving) and nutritional yeast in place of cheese.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
Heat olive oil in an oven‑safe skillet over medium heat. Sauté the onion until translucent.
Add red bell pepper and spinach; cook until the spinach is wilted (about 3–4 minutes).
In a bowl, whisk together the eggs with salt and pepper; stir in the cherry tomatoes and cheese (if using).
Pour the egg mixture over the veggies in the skillet. Cook for 3–4 minutes on the stovetop until the edges begin to set.
Transfer the skillet to the oven and bake for an additional 10–12 minutes, until the center is fully set.
mealPreppingTip: Store individual slices in airtight containers in the fridge. Reheat in the microwave or on the stovetop.

title: Peanut Butter Banana Toast
ingredients: 1–2 slices whole grain or gluten‑free bread
2 tbsp natural peanut butter (or sunflower seed butter for nut allergies)
substitutions: Use sunflower seed butter or another nut‑free spread for those with nut allergies.
instructions: Toast the bread slices to your desired level of crispiness.
Spread peanut (or seed) butter evenly over the toast.
Arrange banana slices on top.
Drizzle with honey and sprinkle a little cinnamon if desired, then serve immediately.
mealPreppingTip: Pre-slice the bananas with a squeeze of lemon juice to prevent browning, and store in an airtight container.

title: Fresh Fruit Salad with Mint & Lime Dressing
ingredients: 3 cups mixed fresh fruits (such as berries, melon, kiwi, grapes, and apple), diced
¼ cup fresh mint leaves, chopped
instructions: In a large bowl, combine all the diced fruits.
In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, honey (if using), and chopped mint.
Drizzle the dressing over the fruit and gently toss to combine.
mealPreppingTip: Store the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For best texture, add the dressing just before serving.

title: Egg and Veggie Breakfast Quesadillas
ingredients: ½ cup shredded cheese (or dairy‑free cheese)
substitutions: Use gluten‑free tortillas and dairy‑free cheese as needed.
instructions: Scramble the eggs in a skillet until just set and set aside.
Wipe the pan clean and heat one tortilla over medium heat.
Sprinkle half the cheese on one side of the tortilla, add the scrambled eggs, sautéed spinach, and diced bell peppers.
Fold the tortilla in half and cook until golden and the cheese is melted (about 2–3 minutes per side).
Slice into wedges and serve with salsa or hot sauce.
mealPreppingTip: After cooling, wrap each quesadilla in foil and store in the fridge. Reheat in a toaster oven or microwave when ready to eat.

title: Whole Grain Blueberry Muffins
ingredients: 1½ cups whole grain flour (or a gluten‑free flour blend)
⅓ cup unsalted butter (melted) or coconut oil
substitutions: Use a gluten‑free flour blend, dairy‑free milk, and coconut oil for a dairy‑free version.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a muffin tin with paper liners.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, beat the eggs and stir in the milk, maple syrup, melted butter (or coconut oil), and vanilla extract.
Mix the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients until just combined.
Gently fold in the blueberries.
Divide the batter evenly among the muffin cups and bake for 18–20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
mealPreppingTip: Muffins can be kept in the fridge for up to 5 days or frozen for longer storage.

title: Sweet Potato Hash with Poached Eggs
ingredients: 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and diced into small cubes
Salt, pepper, and ½ tsp paprika, to taste
substitutions: For an egg-free version, substitute with a tofu scramble or plant‑based egg alternative.
instructions: In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add the diced sweet potatoes, red bell pepper, and onion.
Season with salt, pepper, and paprika; sauté for 10–15 minutes until the sweet potatoes are tender and lightly caramelized.
While the hash cooks, bring a small pot of water to a gentle simmer. Add a splash of vinegar, create a whirlpool, and gently slide in each egg to poach (about 3–4 minutes per egg).
Serve the hash topped with the poached egg(s) and garnish with chopped parsley.
mealPreppingTip: Sweet potato hash can be made ahead and stored in the fridge. Reheat and top with a freshly poached or reheated egg when ready to serve.

title:
Quick Acai 
 Bowl
ingredients: 2 frozen acai puree packs (available at health food stores)
½ cup plant‑based milk (or dairy‑free milk)
Toppings: granola, sliced kiwi, coconut flakes, chia seeds, additional banana slices
substitutions: Use a nut‑free granola and ensure your milk choice suits your dietary needs.
instructions: In a blender, combine the frozen acai packs, frozen banana, berries, and plant‑based milk. Blend until smooth.
Pour the acai mixture into a bowl.
Arrange your chosen toppings in an attractive pattern on top.
mealPreppingTip: Prepare the acai base fresh in the morning for the best texture; pre-portion toppings into small containers for a quick assembly.

title: Muesli with Fresh Fruit and Yogurt
ingredients: 1 cup muesli (store‑bought or homemade; select nut‑free if needed)
1 cup Greek yogurt or dairy‑free alternative
½ cup chopped fresh fruit (berries, apples, bananas)
allergenWarning:
Contains dairy 
and may include nuts
substitutions: Choose non‑dairy yogurt and nut‑free muesli if required.
instructions: In a bowl or jar, add the muesli.
Top with the yogurt and then the chopped fresh fruit.
Drizzle with honey or maple syrup if desired; mix before eating.
mealPreppingTip: Assemble in portable jars for a nutritious, grab‑and‑go breakfast.

title:
Avocado Egg 
 Bake
ingredients: 1 ripe avocado, halved and pitted (scoop out a little extra to enlarge the cavity)
Optional: chopped chives or cilantro, hot sauce, or a sprinkle of bread crumbs for texture
substitutions: For an egg-free version, consider a tofu scramble served in avocado halves.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C).
Carefully scoop a bit more out of each avocado half to create more room for the egg.
Place the avocado halves in a small baking dish.
Crack one egg into each avocado half; season with salt and pepper.
Bake for 12–15 minutes until the egg white is set and the yolk reaches your desired consistency.
mealPreppingTip: While best enjoyed fresh for ideal texture, you can prepare the avocado halves ahead of time and add the egg just before baking.
